blocks.text: Genesis 5 stands within the universal-origins material of Genesis 1–11, where creation, genealogy, flood, and city-building appear before the book turns in chapters 12–50 to the story of one ancestral family and finally Jacob’s household in Egypt. These opening chapters also belong to an ancient Near Eastern literary environment in which similar subjects were discussed. Such parallels can clarify shared motifs and cultural questions, but they do not by themselves prove that Genesis copied another work or determine how Genesis should be interpreted. Questions about the book’s literary formation remain disputed because Genesis does not narrate its own composition.
